Reference Number: POC-CFA5B97DE7-76391
Date of Notice: 2026-08-08
Requested Service/CPT Code: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy/meniscus surgery), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-08. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-04, and I am submitting well within that deadline.

**Stated reason for denial:** The notice states that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." The notice does not specify, in the text provided to me, which particular clinical indication was found to be unmet. I am requesting, as part of this appeal, that Anthem provide me and Dr. Lindqvist's office with the specific clinical criterion or criteria relied upon in this denial, including the exact section of the applicable guideline document, so that we may respond to it directly. I have identified the guideline that Anthem's musculoskeletal-surgery review vendor, Carelon Medical Benefits Management, applies to joint surgery requests — the "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines for Musculoskeletal Surgery: Joint Surgery" (version effective 11/15/2025) — but I was not able to obtain the full text of its knee-arthroscopy-specific indications, and I want to be transparent that I am not quoting or attributing any knee/meniscus-specific criteria language to the plan below, because I have not verified that language directly. Where I do quote the guideline, it is limited to the general "Clinical Appropriateness Framework" language that I was able to retrieve directly from the document itself.

**Response to the denial, mapped to my clinical record:**

1. **Confirmation of diagnosis through complete clinical evaluation.** The general clinical guideline states that appropriateness review requires that "the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient," including "a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention." This has been satisfied:
   - MRI of the knee (2026-06-21) confirmed a **displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking**, with preserved articular cartilage and only Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes.
   - Physical examination documented **positive provocative testing** on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
   - I report ongoing **locking and giving way**, and I am unable to squat or kneel and am limited to level walking.

2. **Failed conservative management prior to surgical request.** My record documents an extended, structured course of non-surgical treatment prior to the surgical request:
   - **14 months** of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest.
   - **16 weeks of supervised physical therapy** (2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06), 16 visits completed, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - **6 months of NSAID therapy** with inadequate relief.
   - A **corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-20**, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms recurred.
   This treatment course reflects a sustained, good-faith attempt at conservative management that has not resolved my mechanical symptoms.

3. **Net benefit and likelihood of improved outcome.** The guideline further states that appropriateness requires that "the anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms" and that "there exists a reasonable likelihood that the intervention will change management and/or lead to an improved outcome for the patient." In my case:
   - I have a structurally confirmed, mechanical lesion (a displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear causing locking) rather than diffuse degenerative disease — my cartilage is preserved and my osteoarthritis grade is mild (Kellgren-Lawrence 1).
   - Locking and instability of this type are mechanical problems that, in my understanding, are not expected to resolve with additional physical therapy, medication, or injections, since the torn meniscal fragment itself is physically blocking normal joint motion.
   - I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, so there are no medical contraindications to surgery.

4. **Request for specific criteria and peer-to-peer review.** Because the denial notice does not identify which specific criterion of the applicable medical policy was not met, I am requesting that Anthem and/or Carelon Medical Benefits Management:
   - Identify the exact provision(s) of the "Joint Surgery" guideline (or any other medical policy applied) that formed the basis for this denial;
   - Provide Dr. Lindqvist's office with an opportunity for a peer-to-peer review, given that the general framework of the guideline appears — based on the clinical facts above — to support medical necessity; and
   - Reconsider the denial in light of the documented failure of 16 weeks of physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection, together with imaging-confirmed mechanical pathology (displaced bucket-handle tear with locking).

**Enclosures submitted in support of this appeal:**
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06, 16 visits)
- Medication/treatment history documenting 6 months of NSAID use and corticosteroid injection (2026-05-20)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-21
- Office visit/examination notes documenting provocative testing and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, MD [attach if available]
- [Any additional records not listed above]

I respectfully request that this appeal be reviewed by a qualified orthopedic or musculoskeletal specialist who has not previously reviewed this request, as is my right under the plan's appeal procedures. Please send all correspondence regarding this appeal, including the specific policy criteria applied and the outcome of this review, to the address and phone number listed above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

Quinn Hayes
Member ID: W991965754

cc: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [office address/fax, if to be copied]
